# Quiz

> Small games at https://quiz.neorgon.com/: count the beats of a loanword, pick
> the sound of a kana, match two columns, put a song line back in order. One
> JSON set per game, every wrong answer explained. Any site can embed a game in
> an iframe and read the answers back over postMessage. Nothing is uploaded.

## Writing a set file

Produce ONE JSON object in the `neo-quiz-set/1` format:

    {
      "format": "neo-quiz-set/1",
      "id": "jp-loanwords-beats",
      "version": "2026-09-04",
      "game": "beats",
      "name": { "en": "Loanword beats", "es": "Pulsos de préstamos" },
      "lang": "ja",
      "skill": "jp.mora.count",
      "licence": { "spdx": "CC-BY-4.0", "screen": "required",
                   "attribution": "Word list by ...", "source": "https://..." },
      "items": [ ... ]
    }

Top-level fields:

- format (required) "neo-quiz-set/1"
- id (required) starts with a letter or digit, then letters, digits, dot, dash,
  underscore. Scores are keyed by it, so never change it on an existing set
- version (required) a YYYY-MM-DD date, bumped on any content change
- game (required) one of beats, sound, pairs, order. A set serves one game
- name (required) a string or { "en", "es" }. English is the fallback, then
  Spanish; "es": null means not translated
- lang (optional) BCP 47 tag of the content, default "ja"
- skill (optional) a dotted string echoed on every quiz:answer unless the URL
  gives ?skill=. With neither, the skill is "quiz.<game>"
- licence (required) { spdx (required, an SPDX id or "public-domain"), screen
  (required, "required" or "none"), attribution (the exact on-screen wording,
  required when screen is "required"), source (URL, optional) }. When screen
  is "required" the attribution renders under the round on every screen that
  shows the set, in the embed too, with source linked beside it
- items (required) at least 1, ids unique within the set, id in the same
  character set as the set id. Shapes per game below

No field may contain markup: a "<" followed by a letter anywhere is an error.
Every learner-facing string is a bilingual value; a bare string is English.

### beats

    { "id": "bag", "word": "bag", "kana": "バッグ", "romaji": "baggu",
      "beats": 3, "split": ["バ", "ッ", "グ"], "rule": "sokuon",
      "explain": { "en": "A small っ is a beat of its own, a held stop.",
                   "es": "La っ pequeña es un pulso propio, una pausa sostenida." } }

- word: the source word, shown under the kana before the answer
- kana: what is counted, shown large. romaji is shown only after the answer,
  because "baggu" spells out the count
- beats: an integer from 1 to 9 equal to split.length. The options are four
  ascending numerals around it, so a word past 9 beats needs another game
- split: the kana cut into beats; joined with "" it must equal kana
- rule: a short code naming the rule (sokuon, long-vowel, n, plain, ...), for
  set authors and the results screen; explain is its one-line human reading

### sound

    { "id": "ki", "kana": "き", "sound": "ki", "row": "k", "column": "i",
      "distractors": ["ka", "sa", "ni"] }

- kana and sound: the two faces. The engine asks in either direction, chosen
  per item by seed
- row: a label shared by the kana of one row; column: "a", "i", "u", "e", "o",
  or null (ん only). The feedback strip is built from the set's items sharing
  row, ordered a i u e o, so a row works when the set carries all five
- distractors (optional) sounds, 3 or more, drawn from when present; otherwise
  three sounds from the same row or the same column in the set

### pairs

    { "id": "inu", "left": "いぬ", "right": "dog", "note": "inu" }

- left and right are the only things on the board. Neither may contain the
  other after trim, casefold and strip-accents, and they may not be equal:
  that is what keeps the answer off the visible text. note (optional) is shown
  only in the feedback after a miss
- a board is four pairs; the set needs at least 4 items and no two rights may
  be equal after the same folding

### order

    { "id": "sakura-1", "tokens": ["さくら", "さくら", "野山も", "里も"],
      "line": "さくら さくら 野山も 里も",
      "gloss": { "en": "Cherry blossoms, cherry blossoms, over hills and villages",
                 "es": "Flores de cerezo, flores de cerezo, por montes y aldeas" } }

- tokens: the correct order, 3 to 9 pieces (keys 1 to 9 are the bank), no
  two of them equal: two pieces is a coin flip and two identical pieces have
  no wrong order. Split a longer line into two items; merge a repeated piece
  with its neighbour ("よい よい")
- line: the display of the correct line; equals tokens joined with "" or " "
- gloss: shown after a miss and on the results screen, never before

### Where a fetched set is stored

Scores for a set fetched from ?set= on an origin other than neorgon.com or one
of its subdomains are keyed `ext:<first 12 hex of SHA-256 of the URL>:<id>`, so
a third-party document claiming a built-in id cannot merge into it. Built-in
sets and *.neorgon.com sets keep their plain id. `setId` carries that key.

## URL parameters

    https://quiz.neorgon.com/?game=beats&set=jp-loanwords-beats&limit=10

- game=beats | sound | pairs | order. Optional when set is given: the set's
  own game is used. An unknown name is quiz:error { code: "game-unknown" };
  a set whose game differs is { code: "game-mismatch" }
- set=<id> a built-in set from data/sets/index.json, or an https URL fetched over
  CORS. Plain http://localhost is accepted only when the engine itself is on
  localhost. Absent in embed: quiz:error { code: "no-set" }. Absent
  standalone: the library
- embed=1 strips the chrome to a slim bar with an "Open in Quiz" link that
  preserves the other parameters except embed and skill, and starts the round
  on load
- limit=<N> items per round, default 10, capped at the set's length. A value
  that is not a finite positive integer is discarded
- seed=<string> makes the shuffle, the numeral window and the sound direction
  deterministic, so a host can replay a round. Default: random per load
- lang=en | es. Absent: the saved preference, then the browser, then en
- skill=<dotted> overrides the set's skill on every quiz:answer
- theme=<name> is read by the fleet's pre-paint theme script, as on every site

## Embedding (iframe)

Contract version `neo-quiz-embed/1`.

    <iframe src="https://quiz.neorgon.com/?embed=1&game=beats&limit=10&set=https%3A%2F%2Fexample.com%2Fbeats.json"
      width="100%" height="560" loading="lazy" style="border:0"
      title="Loanword beats · Quiz"></iframe>

### Messages the engine sends you

Every message is `{ v: 1, type, ... }` and is posted to your origin (the
referrer's origin), never `*`. With no referrer the engine posts nothing.
**Ignore any message whose `v` you do not recognise.** chosen and expected are
always strings.

- quiz:ready `{ setId, setVersion, game, name, total, store }`. total is the
  round length after limit. store is "engine" when this frame writes
  quiz:scores:v1 and "ephemeral" when it does not (see the allowlist). Fires
  once the set resolved, and again every time you send quiz:hello
- quiz:answer `{ setId, game, itemId, skill, correct, ms, chosen, expected }`,
  one per item. In pairs one per pair, decided by the first attempt on that
  left item; later taps that resolve it record nothing. ms is from the item's
  first paint (in pairs, from the previous lock) to the commit
- quiz:session-end `{ setId, game, answered, correct, wrong, ms, medianMs,
  bestStreak, total, complete }`. Fires once per round, when the results
  screen renders. total is the round length; complete is false when the
  learner left the round early (embed only: Leave shows a partial results
  screen and records no score), so a host that marks an exercise finished
  should check it, or answered against total, before doing so
- quiz:error `{ code, message }`. Codes: no-set, set-fetch-failed,
  set-invalid, game-unknown, game-mismatch. The frame shows its own message
  either way; this lets you fall back
- quiz:resize `{ height }`, debounced 120ms. Clamp it; the frame does not

**If you stop receiving quiz:answer, nothing looks broken.** The frame keeps
showing a working game and you quietly stop recording. That is why every
message carries a version and why silence after quiz:ready is a fault.

### Messages you can send the engine

Every inbound message must carry `v: 1` and a `type` starting with `quiz:`;
anything else is dropped without a reply. All three are accepted from any
origin: they are read-only or round-scoped.

- quiz:hello `{ v: 1 }`. The engine re-emits quiz:ready. **Send this on the
  iframe's load event**: the engine can be ready before your listener exists
- quiz:start `{ limit?, seed? }`. Starts or restarts a round
- quiz:theme `{ theme }`. Up to 32 letters, digits, `_` or `-`, applied to
  documentElement.dataset.theme

    const QUIZ = 'https://quiz.neorgon.com';
    window.addEventListener('message', (e) => {
      if (e.origin !== QUIZ || e.source !== frame.contentWindow) return;
      const m = e.data;
      if (!m || m.v !== 1) return;
      if (m.type === 'quiz:ready')  { if (m.store === 'ephemeral') warnNotSaved(); }
      if (m.type === 'quiz:answer') { record(m.itemId, m.skill, m.correct, m.ms); }
    });
    frame.addEventListener('load', () => {
      frame.contentWindow.postMessage({ v: 1, type: 'quiz:hello' }, QUIZ);
    });

### The origin allowlist, and the one invariant

Nothing a host can send writes storage, so the allowlist decides one thing:
whether an embedded frame persists at all. At boot the engine takes the
referrer's origin and asks

    allowed(origin, self) =
         origin === "https://neorgon.com"
      || origin ends with ".neorgon.com" over https      // label boundary, not substring
      || (self is http://localhost:* or http://127.0.0.1:*
          and origin is http://localhost:* or http://127.0.0.1:*)

An allowed host gets store "engine": the round is written to quiz:scores:v1
on quiz.neorgon.com, so a game played inside runcible.neorgon.com shows up in
the library's last score (a same-site guarantee only: browsers partition
third-party storage by top-level site, and Safari may partition even this
case). Any other host, or no referrer, gets store "ephemeral": nothing is
written, and the "Open in Quiz" link is the path that always persists.

**The invariant, stated once: an unlisted origin can never cause a write to
quiz.neorgon.com's persistent storage.** The localhost clause is gated on the
engine itself being local, so it is dead code in production; it exists so
http://localhost:8878 (Runcible) can embed http://localhost:8880 (Quiz) for
real. It is a pure function, `isAllowedOrigin(origin, selfOrigin)` in
js/origin.js, copied from rappel-site with the label-boundary check, and
tools/test-origin.mjs must cover at least Rappel's cases: runcible.neorgon.com
and neorgon.com over https allowed; evil-neorgon.com (the suffix bug),
neorgon.com.evil.io, xneorgon.com, a trailing-dot host, the apex over http,
"null", "", a URL with a path, query or credentials, file:, data:, javascript:,
undefined and a non-string refused; http://localhost:8878 allowed only when
self is http://localhost:8880, and https://localhost, localhost.evil.io and a
LAN address refused even then. The same file carries isAllowedSetSrc (https, or
localhost when the engine is local) and namespacedSetId (the ext: rule).

## The game module interface

Every game is one ES module in js/games/<id>.js, under 500 lines, and exports

    export default {
      id: 'beats',
      name: { en: 'Beats', es: 'Pulsos' },
      describe: { en: 'How many beats does this word have?', es: '...' },
      keys: [],
      mount(host, round, api) { /* render one item */ return { destroy() {} }; }
    }

- id equals the file name and the set's game; name and describe are what the
  library and the round header show
- keys lists the keys the module binds beyond the digits (order: ["Backspace"]).
  They appear in the ? sheet and are refused if reserved (?, h, g). The module
  adds its own listener and removes it in destroy(); digits are the engine's
- mount is called once per item with host emptied. round is
  { items, index, lang, embed }: items is the shuffled round, index the first
  item not yet answered, lang "en" or "es", embed a boolean. A module may
  consume more than one item per mount (pairs takes four from index)
- api is { answer, next, say, t }:
  - answer({ itemId, correct, ms, chosen, expected, why? }) records one
    verdict and posts quiz:answer. why is { text, node? }: text is the one
    sentence the results screen and the live region read, node the rich
    explanation the feedback panel shows (tiles, the row strip, the marked
    line). A wrong answer without why is a defect the engine logs
  - next() says the mount is done. The engine then shows the panel for every
    wrong answer since this mount and advances on Continue, or advances after
    600ms when there were none. Modules never advance themselves
  - say(text) writes to the polite live region
  - t(obj, vars?) resolves a bilingual value by round.lang with English
    fallback and fills {name} placeholders
- options are <button type="button" data-key="N">: the engine binds digits 1
  to 9 and clicks the matching data-key. The shared keycap(n) from js/ui.js
  renders the box beside it; the digit is never in the button's text. beats
  renders no keycaps and gives each numeral tile data-key of its own value

## Storage

- quiz:prefs:v1 `{ v: 1, lang: "en" | "es", round: 5 | 10 | 20, lastGame: <game> | null }`
- quiz:scores:v1 `{ v: 1, rounds: { "<game>/<setId>": { played, last: { correct,
  total, at }, best: { correct, total }, bestStreak } } }`, at in ms
- neither is written in an ephemeral frame; both are read defensively and a
  document with another v is ignored, not migrated

## Runcible: the quiz exercise

    { "id": "e-beats", "type": "quiz", "game": "beats", "skill": "jp.mora.count",
      "src": "books/japanese/sets/jp-loanwords-beats.json", "limit": 10,
      "title": { "en": "Count the beats" } }

- type "quiz" with game (required, one of the four), src (required), skill
  (required), limit (optional positive integer)
- src is a neo-quiz-set/1 document on Runcible's origin and MUST be declared in
  the Book's data[]; an undeclared src is a load error naming book.json, the
  same rule as a deck
- skill is what the host records: every quiz:answer becomes one attempt
  { itemId, skill: spec.skill, correct, ms, answer: chosen, expected } with
  source "quiz". The engine's skill is informational. The skill rule for decks
  applies unchanged: a skill nothing in the Book reads is an error
- the host builds ?embed=1&game=&set=<absolute src>&skill=&lang=&limit= at
  the engine origin (https://quiz.neorgon.com, or http://localhost:8880 when
  the host is on localhost), sends quiz:hello on load, filters on e.origin and
  e.source, drops unknown v, converts session-end into api.done, shouts a
  malformed answer on the page, times eight seconds of silence, and renders an
  "Open in Quiz" link beside the exercise whether or not the frame loaded

## Keyboard

1 to 9 answer. Space or Enter continues. Backspace undoes a piece in order. Esc
asks before leaving a round; R restarts it. `?` sheet, `H` chrome (standalone only), `G` fleet switcher.
